findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/usage-burn-alert-smoke.ts CHK-002:happy:2 evidence note cites the check 'handler: --alert fires with LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_INPUT_TOKENS=1000 override' (L450-468) as covering 'resolveBurnAlertThresholds with LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_INPUT_TOKENS=500000 returns inputTokens=500000 while other defaults are unchanged', but that check never calls resolveBurnAlertThresholds and never uses 500000 -- it only asserts alert-firing behavior with value 1000. The literal value 500000 does not occur anywhere in usage-burn-alert-smoke.ts or usage-burn-alert.ts (grep confirms zero matches). The only resolver test that overrides LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_INPUT_TOKENS to a specific value uses 50000000 (L272-285, 'resolver: each env variable overrides its threshold'), a different untested value. Sibling intents CHK-002:happy:1 (FILE_MB=50->52428800) and CHK-002:happy:3 (AGE_DAYS=14->14) ARE asserted with their exact literal values, so this is a real evidence-note misattribution / coverage gap rather than a stylistic choice.

packages/main/src/tasks/usage-burn-alert-smoke.ts CHK-003:edge:4 requires a session that trips ALL THREE reasons (file-size + input-tokens + session-age) and lists all three in its warning line; no such fixture exists anywhere in the smoke. The only multi-reason fixture (codex-burn-A/HOT, integration check L372-374) is explicitly asserted via assert.deepEqual([...hot.reasons].sort(), ["input-tokens","session-age"], ...) to trip EXACTLY two reasons, never file-size (its transcript is a few hundred bytes, well under the 100MB default). The renderers check (L435-447) constructs a single-reason (input-tokens only) fixture. Evidence notes both for CHK-003:edge:4 ("integration: HOT trips multiple reasons listed together; renderers list reasons joined") and for CHK-001:happy:5 ("evaluator per-reason isolation + edge: all-three-reasons session (doctor fixture)") misdescribe this as a 3-reason test -- there is no 3-reason (doctor) fixture in the file. renderBurnFindingBlock's reasons.join(...) line (core/usage-burn-alert.ts ~L250) is therefore untested with 3 simultaneous reasons.

packages/main/src/tasks/usage-burn-alert-smoke.ts CHK-001:edge:3 requires "A codex session with inputTokens=0 and a claude session with all-zero usage fields are not flagged for input-tokens", but no fixture in the smoke uses a zero-valued codex usage() or an all-zero claude usage object. The nearest row (L352, sessionId 'bbb') has cacheReadInputTokens:2000 (nonzero) and IS flagged, not an example of the intended not-flagged-at-zero case. Existing tests only cover near-threshold (1000) and clearly nonzero (2000/4300/5000/150000000) values. grep across the file confirms no codexUsage(0) call and no all-zero claude usage object anywhere. The evidence note title ("evaluator: zero-usage rows below strictly-greater thresholds are not flagged") does not correspond to any check in the file.
